gappers.catalyst: Drone-component maker bouncing after a ~43% one-month drawdown; no single clean company-specific headline today, with the most recent fundamental news being the Nov 5 Q3 beat (revenue $13.9M, +551% y/y) and an Oppenheimer Outperform initiation at a $30 target.
headlines: Unusual Machines Earnings Call Signals Strong Drone Demand (MarketBeat, Nov 16)
Red Cat, Ondas miss Pentagon Gauntlet II drone finalist cut (scanx.trade, Nov 18)
Company registers to sell 1.93M shares for holders - resale registration, not a new raise (Nov 13)
gappers.catalyst_detail: No verifiable company-specific catalyst was found for today's +10.3% gap. The durable fundamentals are from Nov 5: Q3 revenue of $13.9M, up 551% y/y, with defense and enterprise customers about 90% of sales, and an EPS line reported at (50c) against a (14c) consensus. Oppenheimer initiated at Outperform with a $30 target and Piper Sandler cut its target to $29 from $38 in late October. A Nov 13 registration covering 1.93M holder shares is a resale, not fresh dilution. DATA INTEGRITY FLAG: Alpaca's snapshot and daily bars agree on a $9.61 prior close, but UMAC's live quote is bid $8.23 / ask $11.04, a ~30% spread on a stale 21:00 UTC stamp, and third-party aggregators variously print $13.31, $19.92 and $23.11 for the same sessions. Alpaca is the approved source and is internally consistent, so the gap is reported as-is, but the quote is too wide to trade off.
gappers.why: Mechanically this reads as high-beta drone/defense sympathy inside the broader risk-on bid ahead of the Anthropic IPO debut at 09:30 ET, not as news. A name down ~43% in a month with a 15.6% ATR moves double digits on flow alone, and the Pentagon Gauntlet II finalist cut that hit peers Red Cat and Ondas did not name UMAC, leaving it a relative-strength residual rather than a winner.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day headline-free spike likely to mean-revert. Premarket volume of 3.35M against a 20-day average of 3.04M is roughly one full session's turnover before the open, which is participation, but with no catalyst to anchor it there is nothing to hold the gap. Sector read-through is negative rather than positive: the drone complex just lost a Pentagon selection event, and Red Cat and Ondas are not confirming this move.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: No identifiable catalyst plus a 30%-wide quote means there is no thesis to carry; the Nov 5 earnings beat is two weeks stale and already faded ~43%.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace: the account is flat at 0 positions, so no existing holding competes. The binding constraint is the 3-new-trades-per-week budget, of which 0 are used, and the correlation gate. UMAC fails the 2:1 R:R test at any sane stop: 1 ATR is $1.50, so a 1-ATR stop at $9.10 sits 14.2% below the $10.60 entry, already wider than the mandatory 10% trailing stop, and the 10% trail at $9.54 would sit inside 1 ATR where routine noise takes it out. Clearing 2:1 would require a $13.60 target, a fresh 30%+ advance with no catalyst behind it. Ranks 2-5 are all better-sourced. Do not spend a weekly trade slot here.

gappers.catalyst: B. Riley upgraded AST SpaceMobile from Neutral to Buy with a $48 target, arguing the multi-week selloff had over-priced negative sentiment, and a ULA Vulcan probe cleared Blue Origin's BE-4 engines of fault, removing a launch-risk overhang on AST's New Glenn ride.
headlines: AST SpaceMobile Stock Climbs After B. Riley Upgrade, Analyst Says Rocket Risk Is Priced In (Benzinga)
AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ:ASTS) Stock Rating Raised to Buy at B. Riley Financial (MarketBeat, Nov 19)
ASTS Stock Jumps Overnight Despite New Shares For Engines And Spectrum (Stocktwits)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Two things landed together. B. Riley moved ASTS from Neutral to Buy with a $48 price target, explicitly arguing that negative sentiment was excessively priced in after a punishing multi-week selloff that took the stock to a 52-week low of $25.16 against a 52-week high of $133.86. Separately, the ULA Vulcan failure investigation concluded that Blue Origin's BE-4 engines were not responsible; AST flies on New Glenn, which uses the same engines, so an identified overhang was removed rather than merely deferred. The offsetting negative is real dilution: 10 million shares and $400M issued to Firefly Aerospace for rocket engine technology rights, plus a filing covering 780,052 shares for Ligado Networks and One Dot Six. Other desks are split, with William Blair at Market Perform, UBS and BofA cutting targets, and Berenberg reiterating Buy.
gappers.why: An upgrade-driven short-covering bounce off a 52-week low, amplified because the engine finding retired a specific, nameable risk rather than a vague one. The mechanism is sentiment repair on an oversold, heavily-shorted high-beta name, not a change in cash flows: nothing about revenue or subscriber economics changed overnight.
gappers.impact: Partly sustainable, with a hard near-term test. Premarket volume of 23.0M already exceeds the 18.2M 20-day average, so this is genuine repositioning rather than a thin gap, and an analyst upgrade plus a retired launch risk is more durable than a headline spike. But the dilution overhang that caused the selloff is unresolved, and the move is a bounce off a 52-week low inside a confirmed downtrend. Sector read-through is positive and visible: PL is also gapping, so the whole satellite/space complex is bid together, which cuts both ways because it means neither is moving on its own merits.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The structural catalyst is the nationwide intermittent service activation management still guides to before year-end 2026, a genuine re-rating event; the upgrade and engine clearance are the setup, not the thesis.
gappers.opportunity_cost: This is the best-sourced name on the list and the most defensible use of one of the 3 weekly slots, but it cannot be sized to the rulebook. 1 ATR is $4.06, so a 1-ATR stop at $23.65 sits 14.7% below the $27.71 entry, well outside the mandatory 10% trailing stop, while the 10% trail at $24.94 sits inside 1 ATR and would be taken out by one average day's range. 2:1 R:R off a 1-ATR stop needs $35.83, which is credible against B. Riley's $48 target and the $133.86 52-week high, so the setup clears R:R on reward but fails it on stop placement under the current rules. It also directly displaces PL: both are the same satellite-infrastructure bet, so the >0.75 correlation gate makes these alternatives, not additions. Taking ASTS forfeits PL.

gappers.catalyst: Bloom Energy rebounding with the AI-power complex after Anthropic priced its IPO above range at $83/share, reviving bids for AI datacenter power suppliers following a ~34% drawdown from Oct 13.
headlines: Why Is Bloom Energy Stock Surging Thursday? (Benzinga)
AI Data Centers Don't Have to Wait Years for Power, Bloom Exec Says (Benzinga, Nov 18)
Bloom Energy Falls 4% as Fuel Cell Selloff Deepens (24/7 Wall St, Nov 17)
gappers.catalyst_detail: The proximate trigger is sector-wide: Anthropic priced its IPO above its expected range at $83 per share, which revived interest in AI power suppliers after a brutal stretch in which Bloom fell about 34% between Oct 13 and Tuesday and sits more than 40% below its $351.28 52-week high. Bloom's own fundamentals are strong and recent: NTT DATA agreed to deploy 900 megawatts of its solid oxide fuel cell systems, Bloom will build the fuel cells for a 702-megawatt plant powering Google's Wyoming datacenter, and management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance for the third time to $4.4-4.6B. On Nov 18 Bloom executive Bala Naidu made the core pitch that Bloom can deliver onsite power in months rather than years. Robert W. Baird raised its target to $351 from $310 at Outperform. The bear case is cash: quarterly free cash flow around negative $181M, plus ongoing insider selling.
gappers.why: The Anthropic IPO is a direct demand-signal read-through, not a sentiment accident. The pricing above range at a ~$1.5T valuation validates the scale of AI compute buildout, and the binding constraint on that buildout is grid power, which is exactly what Bloom sells into on a months-not-years timeline. Guidance raised three times plus two named hyperscale deals means the move has fundamentals under it, unlike UMAC.
gappers.impact: The most sustainable catalyst on today's list, but the gap itself is suspect. Premarket volume of 11.5M is well BELOW the 18.5M 20-day average, so this is the thinnest participation relative to normal of any name here and reads as sector beta rather than conviction accumulation. Read-through is unambiguous and confirmed: NBIS is gapping on the identical driver, and the fuel-cell complex of FuelCell Energy and Plug Power has been moving as one block all week. Note the tape risk: Anthropic debuts at 09:30 ET today, so the catalyst is an unpriced event, not a settled one.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Three guidance raises, the 900MW NTT DATA deployment and the Google Wyoming plant are structural contracted demand, and Technology/Industrials is the favored early-cycle sector pairing in the rotation table.
gappers.opportunity_cost: The strongest fundamental case, competing directly with NBIS for the same AI-power exposure, so the correlation gate makes them substitutes. At $182.09 the 20% cap of $20,000 buys 109 shares, so position sizing is not the constraint. R:R is the problem: 1 ATR is $22.46, a 1-ATR stop at $159.63 is 12.3% away versus the 10% trail, and the 10% trail at $163.88 sits inside 1 ATR. A 2:1 target needs $227, which is plausible against the $351 52-week high and Baird's $351 target, so reward is not the binding issue. The honest cost is timing: entering before the Anthropic debut prices in means buying the catalyst at its most uncertain, and a below-average-volume gap is the weakest confirmation on the list. Waiting for the open costs nothing here.

gappers.catalyst: Planet Labs bouncing with the satellite complex after a ~70% six-month decline, with no fresh company news today; the last discrete catalyst was the Nov 9 multi-launch agreement with Stoke Space, and fiscal Q3 2027 earnings land Dec 10.
headlines: Planet Labs Stock Rallies 13%: What's Happening Today? - the Nov 9 Stoke Space multi-launch agreement (Benzinga)
Planet Labs Has Shed 70% Over 6 Months: Two Highly Respected Wall Street Teams Expect Gains Exceeding 250% (24/7 Wall St, Nov 17)
Has Buying Planet Labs Stock Dips Paid Off? (Trefis, Nov 18)
gappers.catalyst_detail: No new company-specific news today; this is sympathy with ASTS and the broader space/satellite group. The most recent discrete catalyst was the Nov 9 multi-launch agreement with Stoke Space, which is building fully reusable rockets, to add launch capacity for Planet's fleet. That spiked the stock 14.5% to a $14.37 close and then fully faded to $12.05 by Nov 18. Fundamentals are mixed but improving: fiscal Q2 2027 revenue was $116M, up 58.1% y/y, though part of that came from a satellite handover that pulled revenue from Q3 into Q2, with Q3 guided to $101-105M and full-year to $430-441M. The stock is still loss-making and fiscal 2027 capex guidance rose to $108M at the midpoint from $87.5M in June. The six-month decline is partly a rotation effect, with investors moving into SpaceX after its IPO.
gappers.why: Pure group beta: ASTS got an upgrade, and PL is the liquid satellite-imagery proxy that moves with it, with the record-IPO backdrop lifting space names generally. There is no PL-specific information in today's move, and the Stoke Space precedent is instructive, since an actual signed launch agreement bought exactly one day before round-tripping completely.
gappers.impact: Most likely a one-day spike that mean-reverts, and the volume agrees. Premarket volume of 5.02M against a 7.28M 20-day average is the weakest absolute participation on the list, under 70% of a normal session. The Nov 9 analogue is the base case: a real catalyst faded inside two weeks, so a catalyst-free bounce should fade faster. Read-through is the ASTS pair; if the ASTS upgrade bounce fails, PL has nothing of its own to stand on.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: No catalyst today, and the Dec 10 fiscal Q3 print is three weeks out, which is too far to carry a no-news gap into and is itself a binary risk event.
gappers.opportunity_cost: PL is the one genuinely interesting structural observation on today's list, and it is about volatility, not the catalyst. At an 8.5% ATR it is the ONLY name here whose 1-ATR stop of $1.03, placing a stop at $11.75 or 8.1% below entry, actually fits INSIDE the mandatory 10% trailing stop. Every other name on this list has a 10% trail sitting inside 1 ATR, meaning the rulebook's own stop would be taken out by routine noise. So PL is the only rules-compatible setup of the five, with a 2:1 target of $14.84 that is below the $14.37 Nov 9 high and well under the $30.27 average analyst target. The catch is that it has the weakest catalyst and the weakest volume, so it is the right structure attached to the wrong reason. It directly displaces ASTS under the correlation gate, and taking the rules-compatible-but-newsless half of that pair over the well-sourced-but-unsizeable half is a real trade-off, not an obvious win. Worth a /trade check if it holds the gap after the open; not worth chasing premarket.

gappers.catalyst: Nebius rallying on AI-infrastructure sentiment repair after strong Nvidia results and the above-range Anthropic IPO pricing, with no Nebius-specific deal announced; the stock had fallen 17% on its own Q3 report and sits ~63% below its June high.
headlines: Nebius Shares Jump After Hours as Nvidia's Strong Quarterly Numbers Lift AI Infrastructure Stocks (Benzinga/TradingView)
CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN Stocks Rise Ahead of Anthropic Debut (GuruFocus)
NBIS, IREN, MRVL Stocks Rally: Nvidia Vows To Keep AI Financing Flywheel Turning, But 'Disciplined' (Stocktwits)
gappers.catalyst_detail: No new Nebius contract; the move is sector-driven on two inputs. Nvidia's strong quarterly results lifted the neocloud group, with Nvidia stating it will keep backing AI buildouts through investments and credit guarantees while describing the approach as selective and disciplined, and its interim CEO noting credit backstops activate only if partners can actually build and deliver the infrastructure. The Anthropic debut ahead of 09:30 ET is the second leg. Nebius's own contracted backlog is substantial but previously announced: a binding deal with AIB Data Centers for 50 MW of critical IT capacity in the southeastern US on an initial 12-year term, a five-year Meta agreement covering $12B of dedicated compute with deliveries beginning early 2027 plus commitments for up to $15B more, and Palantir naming Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner. The damage is also real: the stock fell 17% the day it reported Q3, sits about 63% below its June high, and Citi cut its target to $215 from $265 while keeping a Buy, with analysts citing missed deadlines and heavy interest expense.
gappers.why: A beta-chase in the highest-leverage expression of the AI-compute trade. Nebius is a levered neocloud, so it moves as a call option on AI capex sentiment, and two sentiment inputs landed at once. The Nvidia credit-backstop language matters mechanically because Nebius's bear case is financing cost, so an explicit willingness to backstop partner buildouts relieves the exact pressure point, with the caveat that Nvidia conditioned it on partners delivering.
gappers.impact: Genuine sector repair, but this specific gap is the least confirmed on the list. Premarket volume of 26.6M against a 28.8M 20-day average is below normal, and it follows an after-hours move of roughly 10% on the Nvidia news, so a 5.32% gap is actually a GIVE-BACK from the overnight high rather than a fresh advance, which is the weakest tape structure here. Read-through is broad and confirmed across CoreWeave, IREN and MRVL, and BE is moving on the same Anthropic driver, so this is one trade expressed five ways. The disclosed conflict from the pre-market entry applies: the Anthropic IPO is the catalyst and Anthropic develops the model running this bot.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The Meta $12B five-year agreement, the 12-year AIB contract and the Palantir sovereign-AI designation are structural contracted revenue, and the Nvidia backstop addresses the financing bear case directly; the gap itself is sentiment, but the underlying thesis is multi-quarter.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Competes head-on with BE for the same Anthropic-IPO AI-power exposure, and BE is the better version: BE has three guidance raises and two named hyperscale contracts, while NBIS has a 17% post-earnings drop, missed deadlines and heavy interest expense. Under the >0.75 correlation gate these are substitutes, and spending slots on both would concentrate the book in one factor. R:R is the worst of the five in stop terms: at a 16.5% ATR, 1 ATR is $17.70, so a 1-ATR stop at $94.95 is 15.7% below entry versus the 10% rule, and the 10% trail at $101.39 sits well inside 1 ATR and would be stopped out by half an average day's range. A 2:1 target of $148 is reachable against Citi's $215, so reward is fine and stop placement is the disqualifier. Fading off an overnight high on below-average volume is the worst entry geometry on the list. Prefer BE for this exposure; do not take both.
